title: What the Government Knew
thesis: Rome Statute Article 7 chapeau requires the attack to be carried out 'with knowledge of the attack.' This page is the chronological ledger of every documented warning the federal government received about the demographic, structural, and human-rights consequences of MAID expansion — and ignored. Without this ledger, a hostile reviewer can argue inadvertence. With it, mens rea is on the record.

scenes.headline: What the Government Knew
scenes.subhead: Mens rea ledger. Every warning ignored. Every flag dismissed. The record proves knowledge.

scenes.speaker: Rome Statute, Article 7(1) — Chapeau
scenes.quote: ...committed as part of a widespread or systematic attack directed against any civilian population, with knowledge of the attack.

scenes.speaker: Disability rights coalition (Inclusion Canada, Council of Canadians with Disabilities, et al.)
scenes.speaker_meta: Brief to Standing Committee on Justice and Human Rights, House of Commons, Bill C-7 hearings, November 2020
scenes.quote: Bill C-7 sends a message to people with disabilities that their lives are not worth living. Removing the reasonably foreseeable death safeguard creates a state-administered exit door specifically designed for people whose suffering is socially constructed — poverty, lack of services, isolation — rather than medically irremediable.

scenes.speaker: UN Special Rapporteurs on the rights of persons with disabilities, on extreme poverty, and on the right to health
scenes.speaker_meta: Joint communication to the Government of Canada, January 2021 (during Bill C-7 final reading)
scenes.quote: We are concerned that Bill C-7 will have a discriminatory impact on persons with disabilities and may violate Canada's obligations under the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. The expansion of MAID to people whose death is not foreseeable raises serious concerns about the perception of disability as a fate worse than death.

scenes.speaker: Hon. Lawrence MacAulay, Minister of Veterans Affairs
scenes.speaker_meta: Standing Committee on Veterans Affairs (ACVA) testimony, House of Commons, 2022-12-01
scenes.quote: It is completely unacceptable for any Veterans Affairs Canada employee to suggest medical assistance in dying to a veteran seeking treatment. We have confirmed at least four such incidents.

scenes.speaker: Office of the Chief Coroner of Ontario, MAiD Death Review Committee
scenes.speaker_meta: Vulnerability and MAiD Report, 2024 — submitted to Ministry of Health and to federal Health Canada
scenes.quote: In a substantial subset of Track 2 cases reviewed, the Committee identified that the suffering driving the request was rooted in unmet social needs that the health and social care system had failed to address before the request for MAiD was approved.

scenes.unit: Ontario non-compliance findings reported to federal Health Canada
scenes.context: Cumulative Ontario MAiD compliance reports flag procedural and substantive non-compliance — including inadequate exploration of alternatives, missing safeguards, and same-day approvals — affecting hundreds of provisions. Reports are statutory; federal Health Canada receives them; the federal response has been to expand eligibility, not narrow it.

scenes.speaker: Roger Foley, applicant — Foley v. Victoria Hospital (London, ON)
scenes.speaker_meta: Article 15 communication to Office of the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court, February 2023
scenes.quote: I have been offered medical assistance in dying multiple times. I have not been offered the assisted home care I have been requesting for years. I am being coerced into death by the denial of life. I am asking the Office of the Prosecutor to open a preliminary examination into Canadian state conduct.

scenes.unit: MAID provisions in 2024 — federal Health Canada knew
scenes.context: Health Canada's Fifth Annual Report on Medical Assistance in Dying documents 16,499 provisions in 2024 (5.1% of all Canadian deaths) with Track 2 representing 4.7% of MAID deaths. The report is published by the federal department itself; the data is the federal government's own.

scenes.unit: Track 2 over-representation in lowest material-resources / highest residential-instability quintiles
scenes.context: Ontario MAiD Death Review Committee — Marginalization Data Perspectives report (companion to 2024 Vulnerability Report). Track 2 recipients are massively over-represented in the lowest material-resources quintile (28.4% vs 20% population baseline) and highest residential-instability quintile (48.3%). Per Grok 4 Heavy 2026-04-27 strategic research, this is the primary statistical evidence the state knowingly offers death instead of material support — the textbook Article 7(2)(b) extermination definition: 'the intentional infliction of conditions of life calculated to bring about the destruction of part of a population.'

scenes.headline: What knowledge looks like on the record
scenes.body:
The Article 7 chapeau is satisfied not by inferring knowledge but by reading it off the parliamentary record, the federal department's own annual reports, the statutory provincial coroner reports, and a private Article 15 submission to the ICC OTP.

  • Hansard 2020–21: disability advocates warned during Bill C-7 passage that the bill targeted disabled lives. The bill passed.
  • UN Special Rapporteurs 2021: formal joint communication received by the Government of Canada. The bill passed.
  • VAC 2022: Minister confirmed in committee that at least four MAID-to-veterans incidents occurred. No structural reform followed.
  • Ontario MDRC 2024: statutory reports flag Track 2 vulnerabilities, hundreds of non-compliance findings, demographic skew. Federal expansion continues.
  • Foley 2023: Article 15 communication puts the federal cabinet on direct notice of population-level harm. No MAID restriction follows.

The pattern is: warning, ignored, expansion. That is what mens rea looks like under Article 7.
